title: Sequence-Level Vocal Convergence in Common Marmosets

## Core Question

Do social partners converge not only in the sound of individual calls, but also in the larger sequence structure of their vocal exchanges?

## Approach

This work develops a sequence-comparison framework inspired by bioinformatics-style alignment, then combines it with note-level spectral measurements to test for multiple layers of vocal accommodation.

## What Emerged

The project points to separable forms of encoding: individual identity in spectral call features and dyad identity in sequence-level structure.

## Broader Goal

The larger ambition is to move beyond single-call analysis and treat vocal sequences as structured social behaviour in their own right.
